subject: MedixHealth pilot — deployment options & compliance follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: MedixHealth pilot — deployment options & compliance follow-up

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we discussed
- Primary goal: 6-week pilot to validate PHI-safe ingestion + inference for appointment summarization.
- Compliance needs called out by your security team: HIPAA/BAA, SOC 2 Type II evidence, audit log retention for key events, and AWS us-east-1 residency.
- Deployment modes: we covered Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool), and Private VPC/on-prem (strongest isolation).

Compliance & recommended starting path
- Attached: our latest SOC 2 Type II report and a draft BAA for your legal review.
- Recommendation for pilot: Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 with strict egress controls + signed BAA. This gives predictable throughput for your volume and keeps timelines shorter than a full Private VPC setup.

Outstanding questions I captured
1) Will Medix require an HSM/KMS-backed solution for keys (we can support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private)?
2) Desired audit log retention period (we can extend retention as an add-on).
3) Legal/Procurement contacts and estimated PO timeline.

Next steps
- I will send the BAA and SOC2 report (attached) — please share with legal/security.
- Vivek will follow up with technical checklist and short comparison doc for Dedicated vs Private.
- Proposed timeline: kick off pilot around June 1 if we have BAA signed and PO in place.

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf, redwood_BAA_draft.docx

Thanks — feel free to correct anything I missed.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@medixhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@medixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedixHealth pilot — deployment options & compliance follow-up

Camila —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side after an initial pass: 
- We do require a signed BAA before any PHI flows.
- SOC 2 Type II report is required; if you can point to the specific control mappings (encryption, access logs, incident response) that would speed up our review.
- Must keep data within AWS us-east-1 for the pilot.
- Audit log retention: our auditors are currently recommending 7 years for certain event types. Can Redwood support that retention window?

Technical Q: between Dedicated vs Private VPC, what are the implications for key management and network egress restrictions? Our security lead (cc Rajiv) will want to talk to Vivek directly.

If you can get the BAA over and Vivek's checklist, we can route to legal and aim for a June 1 pilot start, pending PO.

—Emily
Emily Zhang
Director of Security & Privacy | MedixHealth
emily.zhang@medixhealth.com | 617-555-0192

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@medixhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@medixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedixHealth pilot — deployment options & compliance follow-up

Emily / team —

Quick technical notes to address your questions: 
- Key management: Dedicated capacity can use either Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed KMS keys (we support AWS KMS CMKs). Private VPC/on-prem can integrate with HSMs for FIPS 140-2 workloads but requires longer lead time (network configuration + cert exchanges).
- Network egress: Dedicated allows strict egress IP whitelisting and proxy routing; Private VPC gives you full control over networking (peering/VPN) with zero public egress if desired. Hosted API is not a fit for PHI unless covered by an explicit BAA and additional controls.
- Audit logs: our platform collects granular event logs (requests, model version, user id, token counts). Standard retention is 90 days; we offer extended retention tiers up to 10 years as an add-on. We can scope a 7-year retention plan and include export-from-retention for your archival process.
- SOC 2 mapping: attached is a short integration checklist mapping our controls to common SOC domains and recommended evidence collectors for your audits (medix_integration_checklist.xlsx).

Recommendation: Begin with Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 for the pilot (faster provisioning, covered by our SOC 2 scope) plus a signed BAA. If your auditors require on-prem or HSM-backed keys for production, we can plan a phased move to Private VPC in Q4.

Happy to set up a 30-minute technical call with Rajiv and your infra team — availability next week is good for me.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Team —

This all looks good. We would like to proceed with a Dedicated pilot in us-east-1, contingent on: 
- Signed BAA (please send via DocuSign),
- SOC 2 Type II evidence & the integration checklist (received),
- Written confirmation that extended audit log retention (7 years) can be implemented for the event classes we flagged.

If you can get a DocuSign envelope with the BAA and a draft SOW this week, I will take them to procurement. Target start date: June 1, 2025.

Best,
Emily
